prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The monocular depth map captures a steep downward egocentric viewpoint over a woven bamboo-framed cot (~0.5–1.0 m below the camera) and the flat floor beyond it (~1.3–1.6 m away), showing the camera wearer's pink-draped lap and folded right arm as the brightest, nearest surfaces at ~0.3–0.6 m. Within the wearer's immediate arm's reach (~0.4–0.8 m) are a mint-green knitted piece with needles on the left and a yarn ball in the center, while a white cloth, purple fabric, and a second person's striped left arm and hand sit slightly lower and farther to the right on the cot (~0.7–1.0 m from the wearer, ~0.2 m beside the wearer's elbow). Beyond the cot's front-right bamboo rail and above the dark floor plane, a third person's crossed legs and feet in sandals appear in darker grey tones at ~1.2–1.6 m (~0.5 m past the cot edge and second person), with all three people's heads out of view so no gaze toward the wearer is visible, and body orientations indicated only by limbs facing roughly forward or diagonally away from the cot. Across frames 1 to 2, the camera turns and pitches slightly rightward as the wearer's right hand retreats from the knitted fabric on the left to rest across their chest through frame 5, bringing the two people on the right further into the frame while the broom on the floor (~1.3 m away) shifts upward and left. Compared to RGB, the depth map much more clearly separates the elevated cot plane and the wearer's elevated forearm from the recessed floor and resolves the 3D relief of the yarn ball and fine knitting needles, though it is unreliable on the floor where the broom disappears into uniform darkness and in frame 1 where the cot's bamboo rail and rope weave are flattened into a single smooth ramp.
descriptions.segmentation: The instance segmentation map attempts to parse the downward-looking scene into discrete 'person' masks against an unlabelled black background, primarily isolating the camera wearer's torso, pink garment, and right arm in the lower-center foreground (~0.3–0.7 m from the camera, within immediate self-reach). From frame 2 onward, separate masks at the lower-right and upper-right edges mark the partly occluded person sitting beside the wearer on the cot (~0.6–0.9 m away, within arm's reach of the wearer and the white cloth) and the third person seated on the floor beyond the front-right cot rail (~1.2–1.6 m away, ~0.5 m from the cot edge, holding a plastic bag within their own reach in frame 5). As the camera pans slightly rightward after frame 1 and the wearer's right arm moves from the left-side knitting to rest horizontally across their torso in frames 2–5, the right-side person masks expand into view, though all heads remain outside the frame and no one is seen looking toward the camera wearer. While the segmentation masks help distinguish the boundary between the wearer's right shoulder and the adjacent person's arm on the lower right where colorful fabrics visually merge in the RGB image, the map omits all non-person objects including the yarn, knitting needles, cloths, cot, and broom. Furthermore, the segmentation is highly unreliable across frames: it leaves a hollow gap inside the wearer's bent right arm, swaps instance colors between frames, and falsely labels the bamboo cot rail, woven ropes, white cloth, and floor broom as 'person' regions in frames 1, 3, and 5.
descriptions.pose: The pose map renders 2D skeletal keypoints on a black background, detecting no skeletons in frame 1 and only a single magenta hand skeleton for the camera wearer's right hand in frames 2 through 5 at roughly 0.4–0.5 m in front of and below the camera. Across frames 2 to 5, this magenta hand remains stationary on the left side of the wearer's chest—within reach of the nearby yarn ball (~0.5 m away) and knitted fabric to the left—after having retreated from the left edge of the frame between frames 1 and 2 as the camera shifted slightly rightward. In frame 5 only, a yellow body-and-face keypoint skeleton appears on the right side, spanning from the cot surface (~0.7 m away) toward the upper-right floor (~1.3 m away), while the rest of the scene—including the wearer's torso, the cot, the yarn, and the broom on the floor—remains completely unrendered. This sparse skeleton view isolates the exact finger articulation and leftward orientation of the wearer's resting right hand free from the visual clutter of the pink clothing and green wool in RGB. However, the map is largely unreliable for scene-wide spatial understanding because it misses the wearer's hand in frame 1, fails to detect the adjacent person's hand or the floor-seated person's legs and hands in frames 1–4, and in frame 5 hallucinates a single distorted yellow torso-and-head skeleton across the white cloth and adjacent arms where no head is present in the field of view.
